blocks.html: This is for a B2B company with a small list, often a few hundred to a few thousand contacts, where one or two people handle marketing on top of other work.
If you already run HubSpot for sales, you may be weighing its marketing tools against a separate email platform. This page covers the separate-platform side, priced for a small list.

Start with Brevo if you want to send for free while the list is small. Pick Transpond if you want a low monthly price with several users and unlimited automations. Pick ActiveCampaign if automation is the heart of what you do and you're comfortable paying for it.
All three price by list size or email volume, so the number on the pricing page only holds for the list size it was quoted at. Re-price at the size you expect a year from now.

Transpond Starter is $9.90 a month billed annually at 250 contacts, with up to 3 users. Growth is $19.80 a month billed annually at 250 contacts, with up to 5 users and unlimited automations. There's also a free plan for email marketing basics, and annual billing saves up to 10%.
Transpond also offers AI-built branded email templates and an AI content assistant from Starter. One limit to know: Transpond offers an SMS add-on for UK customers only.

Brevo has a free plan with no credit card, sending up to 300 emails a day. Starter is $9 a month on monthly billing, or $97 a year, including the first email tier, and Standard is $18 a month on monthly billing, or $194 a year, including the first email tier. Per Brevo, yearly billing saves 10%.
Seats are tight on the lower plans: Brevo lists 1 marketing seat on Starter and up to 3 on Standard. Contacts are tied to email volume, with 500 contacts at the 5,000-emails-a-month tier on Starter.

ActiveCampaign Starter is $15 a month billed yearly for 1,000 contacts, with 10,000 email sends a month and 1 user seat. Plus is $49 a month billed yearly for 1,000 contacts, adding landing pages and an optional enhanced CRM. Pro is $79 a month billed yearly for 1,000 contacts, with 3 user seats. There's a free 14-day trial.

ActiveCampaign gives you 250+ pre-built email templates and multi-step automation from Starter. The pricing page shows prices that rise with the size of your contact list, so a bigger list moves you up fast.
Count users first. If two or three people need to build campaigns, check the seat limit on the plan before the price. A cheap plan with one seat means sharing a login, which you shouldn't do.
Then list the automations you'll actually build in the first quarter: a welcome series, a demo follow-up, a re-engagement email. If that's the whole list, you don't need the most advanced builder.
Last, decide how contacts move between your CRM and the email tool. If sales lives in HubSpot, look for a sync or an integration before you import a single list.
Set up SPF, DKIM, and DMARC on your sending domain before the first campaign. Every tool here will walk you through it, and skipping it hurts deliverability from day one.
Import only contacts who agreed to hear from you, and keep the unsubscribe link visible.

closing: Pick the cheapest plan that gives every sender a seat and covers the automations you'll build this quarter, then re-price as the list grows.

products.name: Transpond
products.pick: Best fit if you want low prices for a small list, a few users, and unlimited automations on Growth.

products.name: Brevo
products.pick: Best fit if you want a free plan that sends daily and prices driven by email volume.

products.name: ActiveCampaign
products.pick: Best fit if multi-step automation is the main job and you'll pay more for it.
